notes: Perfect claim overlap (C8, C41, C42, C43, C92). Both agree that doxorubicin induces p21 and COL1A1 expression in a CREB3L1-dependent manner. Reviewers acknowledge the gene expression findings without raising concerns.

Near-perfect overlap (94.1% Jaccard) on proteolytic cleavage claims (C6, C7, C20-C36). Both agree that S1P/S2P-mediated cleavage of CREB3L1 is well-demonstrated. LLM includes C40 (SREBP-2 specificity) which reviewers address separately in R9.

50% claim overlap on ceramide mechanism (C3, C4, C65-C67, C78, C85). LLM finds ceramide-CREB3L1 connection well-established through multiple approaches. Reviewers express concerns about lack of literature context, possible myriocin off-target effects, and whether C6-ceramide mimics natural ceramide.

73.3% overlap on doxorubicin sensitivity claims (C9-C11, C45, C49-C55). LLM finds correlation between CREB3L1 and sensitivity well-supported across multiple cell lines. Reviewers acknowledge findings but raise methodological concerns about single shRNA use, single clone analysis, and lack of rescue studies.

75% overlap on biomarker claims (C12, C82, C83). Both agree the clinical biomarker proposal is speculative and requires additional validation. LLM notes difficulty due to combination chemotherapy; reviewers request direct data analysis.

62.5% overlap on etoposide comparison (C58, C59, C61-C63). Both agree the specificity finding is present but incomplete. LLM notes DNA damage ruled out as primary signal. Reviewers note lack of etoposide ceramide measurements leaves mechanistic interpretation incomplete.

26.3% overlap on ceramide experimental approaches (C70, C71, C73, C76, C77). LLM finds pharmacological and exogenous ceramide experiments supportive. Reviewers question whether single approach (myriocin) is sufficient and whether C6-ceramide is appropriate mimetic, requesting alternative confirmation methods.
Minimal overlap (C40 only) on SREBP-2 specificity control. Both accept that doxorubicin selectively activates CREB3L1 but not SREBP-2, demonstrating pathway specificity.
LLM evaluates ceramide trafficking mechanism (C90, C91) as speculative analogy to SREBP-2. No corresponding peer review result addresses these specific mechanistic claims about ER-to-Golgi transport.

Different claim sets but related concepts. LLM addresses broader speculative claims (C93-C95, C103-C105) about master regulator role and therapeutic implications. Reviewers question p53 independence (C97, C98). Both find these broader interpretive claims insufficiently supported.
